summary: Reproduced that candidate 034ffd7a returned fp32 containers containing only bf16-rounded logits, then replaced the aiter cast-after-bf16 path with ROCm torch.mm fp32 output accumulation and added a numerical precision regression covering production, fallback, and skinny shapes. The prepared base's existing GLM-5.2 fp32 correction-bias fixes remain intact.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression at exact candidate behavior: all production, fallback, and skinny subtests found zero output values carrying precision beyond bf16.

Passing-after regression: fp32 dtype, correct shape, finite values, non-bf16-representable logits, and error no worse than a bf16-rounded independent fp32 reference for three boundary shapes; 1 test and 3 subtests passed.
Existing GLM-5.2 correction-bias allocation and routing boundary coverage; 9 tests passed.
On gfx950, corrected max absolute errors versus fp32-input F.linear were 7.16e-7, 4.77e-7, and 2.39e-7; corresponding bf16-rounded reference errors were 7.79e-3, 7.80e-3, and 7.49e-3.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, HIP 7.2.26015; raw logs record the imported source as /job/repo/python/sglang/srt/layers/rocm_linear_utils.py.

remaining_limitations: No GLM-5.2 weights were available; no full-model semantic or accuracy run was performed.
Only one GPU was used; multi-GPU and multi-node behavior were not tested.

Performance against an available tuned aiter production entry was not evaluated; the correction deliberately bypasses aiter for router logits because the observed fallback computes in bf16 before widening.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
